The Industry Brief

Edition No. 9Covering November 9 to 15, 2026Published November 16, 2026

Toyota Revives Scion With a 25 MPH Kei Truck, Honda Bets on Hybrids and BMW Recalls Its Own Fix

Toyota brought back Scion with a mini truck built in Indiana. Honda is spending $3 billion on a plant that can build anything while it writes off its EV plans, Mercedes froze investment at home, BMW told 720,796 owners to park outside because its 2024 repair didn't work, Ford says the first Mach-Es average 92% battery health after about 5 years, global EV sales rose 8%, regulators asked whether Waymo's school-bus fix worked and Rimac ended the Nevera at 71 cars.

By Diana Chambers · 31 minute read

In this edition

  1. Toyota brings back Scion, and its first vehicle is a kei truck that tops out at 25 mph
  2. Honda bets $3 billion on a hybrid-ready plant in Ohio, and the next CR-V will be hybrid-only
  3. Mercedes freezes investment in its German plants and says it must weigh closures
  4. 5 years in, the first Mustang Mach-Es still average 92% battery health, Ford says
  5. BMW tells 720,796 owners to park outside, because the 2024 fix didn't fix it
  6. Global EV sales rise 8%, but Europe, America and China are telling 3 different stories
  7. Regulators ask whether Waymo's school-bus fix worked, and Tesla's robotaxi reaches San Antonio
  8. Rimac ends the Nevera at 71 cars, and Lotus shows the hybrid V8 for its next supercar

The week's theme was the second try. Toyota brought back a brand it retired a decade ago, BMW is recalling cars it already recalled, regulators are checking whether Waymo's recall did its job, and Honda is building a factory that can change its mind after paying for a plan it dropped. Mercedes and its workers are at odds over what a German-built car should cost, and Rimac stopped building a car that set records on the track but not in the showroom. As always, every story carries a status line, because a final count, a forecast and a promise in a press release are not the same kind of news.

New vehicles · Toyota

Shown November 9, announced November 10 · built in Indiana from the second half of 2027 · fleets first, no price yet

Toyota Brings Back Scion, and Its First Vehicle Is a Kei Truck That Tops Out at 25 MPH

The KEI-01 is a Japanese-style mini truck, built in Indiana and sold first to fleets. It can be sold new because it's certified as a low-speed vehicle, which most states allow on roads posted 35 mph or less.

PLANO, Texas — Toyota brought back the Scion name on November 9, a decade after retiring it, as "Scion by Toyota," which it calls a "freedom lab" for new ideas. Its first vehicle, the KEI-01, is a right-hand-drive mini truck with a 660 cc 3-cylinder engine, a CVT, selectable 4-wheel drive and a payload of up to 272 kg (600 lb), in a body just over 11 feet long and under 5 feet wide. It's built to FMVSS No. 500, the federal standard for low-speed vehicles, which limits it to 25 mph. Toyota Indiana will assemble it from the second half of 2027, with a $34 million investment and about 50 new jobs, and it'll be sold first to fleets through selected Toyota dealers. Toyota "may consider expanding availability to limited retail sales at a later date," it said, and gave no price or horsepower. It didn't say what the truck is based on, though several outlets identify it as the Toyota Pixis Truck sold in Japan, itself a Daihatsu Hijet. The first Scion brand ran from 2003 to 2016 and sold 1,092,675 cars through 2015.

The 25 mph limit is the trade-off that makes it possible. A low-speed vehicle needs only basic equipment, such as headlamps, turn signals, mirrors, seat belts, a windshield and a rear camera, not the crash tests and airbags a regular car must pass. Most states let low-speed vehicles use roads posted 35 mph or less. Americans have been importing old kei trucks for years, but they can only be brought in once they're 25 years old, and several states have refused to register them. "Scion by Toyota gives us a place to challenge conventional thinking, explore new possibilities and create mobility in new ways," said Simon Humphries, Toyota's chief branding officer.

The Carveyance take

Americans fell for kei trucks the hard way: 25-year-old imports, state DMVs and the occasional revoked registration. Toyota's is new, under warranty and built in Indiana, but it gives up the one thing an old import can do on a back road: keep up with traffic. That makes it a ranch, campus and job-site tool, not a tiny Tacoma. If fleets like it, the retail question gets interesting.

What to watch: the price, the horsepower, and whether Toyota opens sales to individual buyers.

Hybrids and earnings · Honda

Plant announced November 9 · results November 10 · CR-V news November 12 · production is expected to start in 2029, pending final government approvals

Honda Bets $3 Billion on a Hybrid-Ready Plant in Ohio, and the Next CR-V Will Be Hybrid-Only

The new plant is expected to build up to 240,000 vehicles a year from 2029. Honda is paying for it while still writing off its EV plans: another ¥484.8 billion (about $3.1 billion) in 3 months.

MARYSVILLE, Ohio — Honda said on November 9 it will spend $3 billion on a new auto plant between its Marysville and East Liberty factories, its fourth in Ohio, with capacity for 240,000 vehicles a year and more than 2,000 jobs. Production is expected to start in 2029, "pending final government approvals." It will be able to build hybrids, gasoline cars and EVs, and Honda didn't name the models. It also said it will convert a line at its Ohio transmission plant to build hybrid systems, raising that capacity 250%, add a line for larger hybrid systems in Georgia and build a new V6 hybrid engine in Alabama. Honda's US capacity will rise to about 1.3 million vehicles a year. "We are making one of the most significant commitments in our history to position Honda for the next 50 years," said Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda.

TOKYO — The next day, Honda said its operating profit for July to September fell 39.2% to ¥117.9 billion (about $746 million), after ¥484.8 billion of EV-related losses, mostly money set aside to compensate suppliers for EV models it canceled. Without them, operating profit more than doubled, to ¥602.8 billion (about $3.8 billion). Honda raised its full-year operating-profit forecast 20%, to ¥780 billion (about $4.9 billion), on strong motorcycle sales and more cars sold in North America. On November 12, it said the next CR-V, due next year, will come only as a hybrid. Hybrids are already more than half of CR-V sales and about 30% of Honda-brand sales in America.

The Carveyance take

For 5 years, the biggest factory announcements in America were about batteries. Honda's biggest in years is a plant that can build anything, and the cars it's naming are hybrids. It's still paying for the EV plan it dropped, which may be the most expensive lesson in the business right now: build the factory that can change its mind.

What to watch: which models the new Ohio plant builds, and the new CR-V's reveal.

Industry · Germany

Mercedes' freeze reported November 12, from an interview posted for employees · no plant named for closure · VW's buyout window opens November 16

Mercedes Freezes Investment in Its German Plants and Says It Must Weigh Closures

Talks on cutting labor costs stalled, and Mercedes says a production hour in Germany costs up to 5 times as much as in Eastern Europe. Volkswagen, meanwhile, is offering up to €264,000 (about $296,000) for people to leave, a German magazine reported.

STUTTGART, Germany — Mercedes-Benz's board has "jointly decided to halt all further investments in our German locations," production chief Michael Schiebe said in an interview posted for employees on November 12, after talks with the works council and the IG Metall union on cutting labor costs failed to produce a deal. No plant has been named. "We all want to avoid plant closures at all costs," said Britta Seeger, the board member for human resources. "Unfortunately, however, we must now explore this option in more detail." Schiebe first warned in September that without savings Mercedes would have to close 1 German assembly plant and 1 powertrain plant; it builds cars in Sindelfingen, Bremen and Rastatt. Mercedes says a production labor hour in Germany costs up to 5 times as much as at its Eastern European sites, and chief executive Ola Källenius has put it as an index: Germany 100, the US 80, Hungary 30 and Romania 20. He wants Germany at 80. Management wants a longer working week without more pay, against the 35-hour week IG Metall defends. Mercedes' car division earned an adjusted €560 million (about $627 million) in the third quarter, half what it made a year earlier.

WOLFSBURG, Germany — Volkswagen opens a new round of buyouts on November 16, Manager Magazin reported: up to €209,000 (about $234,000), depending on pay grade and years of service, plus €55,000 (about $62,000) more for staff who register interest by December 4. VW agreed in 2024 to cut more than 35,000 jobs in Germany by 2030, and new in-house wage talks with IG Metall start November 24. BMW, meanwhile, canceled shifts this week because of what it called short-term bottlenecks in external parts supply. It didn't name the part, and unnamed company sources told dpa the plants were Regensburg, Leipzig and Oxford.

The Carveyance take

Germany's carmakers built their country's middle class on cars that sold at premium prices around the world. Those prices are under pressure in China, and the cost of building at home isn't. Mercedes isn't threatening to leave Germany so much as telling its workers what the spreadsheet says, and the next few months of talks will decide how much of it they accept.

What to watch: whether Mercedes and IG Metall reach a deal, and how many VW workers take the buyout by December 4.

Electric vehicles · Ford

Ford's own data, published November 9 · not independently audited · Ford didn't say how many packs were replaced

5 Years In, the First Mustang Mach-Es Still Average 92% Battery Health, Ford Says

Ford's data on more than 36,000 model-year 2021 cars is one of the largest looks yet at how an American EV's battery ages. The batteries are holding up far better than the cars' resale values.

DEARBORN, Mich. — Ford says the more than 36,000 Mustang Mach-Es from the 2021 model year, its first, keep an average of 92% of their usable battery capacity after an average ownership period of 5.2 years and 2 billion miles. "Ninety-five percent of those vehicles fall between 87% and 97% health," wrote Kevin Vander Laan, Ford's technical leader for high-voltage battery cells and systems. More than 2,000 owners have passed 100,000 miles on their original battery and average better than 91%, and the 30-plus drivers past 200,000 miles average 88%. As a rough guide, 92% of the 300-mile EPA range of a 2021 extended-range, rear-drive Mach-E is about 276 miles, though range also depends on weather and speed.

The figures come from Ford's own connected-car data, and Ford didn't say how it calculates battery health, how many packs have been replaced, or how the results vary with climate and fast charging. Independent data points the same way. Geotab, which studied more than 22,700 EVs, reported in January that batteries lose about 2.3% of their capacity a year on average, and about 1.5% in cars that seldom use the fastest chargers. The money tells a different story: 5-year-old EVs had lost 57.2% of their value, against 41.8% for all cars, in iSeeCars' study this year, and the Mach-E had lost 60.8%.

What 5 years did to the Mach-E

The Carveyance take

Shoppers worry that a 5-year-old EV is like a 5-year-old phone. Ford's numbers, and Geotab's, say the battery isn't the problem. The price is: EVs start expensive and lose value faster than the cars around them. That's bad news for the first owner and good news for the second.

What to watch: whether Ford publishes the same data for later model years and for the F-150 Lightning, broken down by battery and climate.

Safety · BMW

NHTSA's warning November 13 · recall 26V733, filed November 4 · the new repair is still being developed · owner letters and VIN lookup from December 25

BMW Tells 720,796 Owners to Park Outside, Because the 2024 Fix Didn't Fix It

The same 2012–2018 BMWs recalled in 2024 for a water-pump connector that can short circuit and catch fire are being recalled again. The new repair isn't ready yet.

WASHINGTON — NHTSA told owners of 720,796 BMWs on November 13 that "you should park your vehicle outside and away from buildings and other vehicles until the vehicle is repaired." An improperly sealed electrical connector on the engine's electric water pump can let in moisture and short circuit, which raises the risk of a fire even when the car is parked and off. The recall covers the 228i, 328i, 428i and 528i and their xDrive versions, the 28i versions of the X1, X3, X4 and Z4, and the X5 xDrive40e plug-in hybrid, from the 2012 to 2018 model years. The biggest group is the 2012–2016 3 Series sedan, with 236,702 cars.

It's the same group of cars BMW recalled in August 2024, when the fix was a shield to keep crankcase fluid off the connector. BMW now says the connector's plastic can become brittle over time and let moisture in anyway. It knows of about 10 incidents in America "that relate, or may relate" to the problem in cars that already had the 2024 repair, and no crashes or injuries have been reported. BMW estimates that fewer than 0.1% of the cars have the defect. The new repair is "in development" and will be free. Letters go out from December 25, the same day the cars' VINs become searchable at nhtsa.gov/recalls. And by the end of September, only about 40.5% of the cars had received the 2024 repair, according to BMW's latest report to NHTSA.

The Carveyance take

A recall is supposed to end with a safe car. 2 years after the first one, these owners have a fix that may not have worked, a new one that doesn't exist yet and instructions to keep the car out of the garage until it does. If you own one, check your VIN and follow the parking advice. If you're shopping for one used, more than half of these cars never got even the first repair.

What to watch: when BMW's new repair is ready, and whether NHTSA's next quarterly reports show owners getting it faster than last time.

Electric vehicles · The world

Benchmark Mineral Intelligence's October figures, November 12 · China's, November 11 · the counts include plug-in hybrids

Global EV Sales Rise 8%, but Europe, America and China Are Telling 3 Different Stories

Europe is up 36%. North America's gain is mostly an easy comparison. China's home market is shrinking, so its carmakers exported a record 606,000 new-energy vehicles.

LONDON — Buyers worldwide bought 2.09 million electric cars and plug-in hybrids in October, 8% more than a year earlier, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reported on November 12. Europe rose 36%, to 510,000, and in Germany they passed 45% of sales. North America rose 24% to 130,000, about 110,000 of them in the US, its first year-over-year gain this year. Benchmark said that's because October 2025 was the first month after the federal tax credit expired, on September 30, 2025: "The return to growth therefore reflects the easier comparison base more than a recovery in demand." China fell 12% to 1.14 million, and the rest of the world rose 85% to 300,000.

BEIJING — China's carmakers sent more abroad. Exports of new-energy vehicles, which China counts as battery EVs, plug-in hybrids and range extenders, commercial ones included, rose about 140% in October to a record 606,000, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers said on November 11. That's almost a third of the new-energy vehicles they sold. Chinese carmakers' total sales, exports included, fell 9.2% to 3.016 million, and sales inside China fell 26.6%.

The Carveyance take

There isn't one EV market anymore. Europe is buying, America has settled at a lower level, and China is building more than its own buyers want and selling the rest to everyone else. When someone says EV sales are booming or collapsing, the useful question is: where?

What to watch: Europe's official October registration figures, and the US share of new-car sales once Cox Automotive publishes October's.

Self-driving · Waymo and Tesla

NHTSA opened the recall query November 6 and made it public November 9 · it's an inquiry, not a finding · Tesla's San Antonio service started November 9

Regulators Ask Whether Waymo's School-Bus Fix Worked, and Tesla's Robotaxi Reaches San Antonio

NHTSA says most of the school-bus passes it found happened after Waymo's software recall. The same day the inquiry became public, Tesla opened its biggest robotaxi zone at launch yet.

WASHINGTON — NHTSA opened a recall query on November 6 into 2,895 Waymo vehicles running its 5th-generation driving system, to "assess the adequacy of the remedy" in the recall Waymo filed last December. That recall covered 3,067 vehicles and fixed software that let a Waymo that had stopped for a school bus, with its red lights flashing or its stop arm out, drive on before the bus was ready. Waymo sent the fix to every car between November 5 and November 17, 2025. But of the incidents NHTSA gathered in its earlier investigation, "a majority of the incidents occurred after the" fix, the agency wrote. Austin's school district had counted 24 violations by mid-January, at least 4 of them after the update, and Atlanta's public schools counted 6. A recall query is how NHTSA checks whether a recall actually worked, and it can lead to a new one. "We have made significant improvements to vehicle behavior around school buses and have received no citations since March 2026," a Waymo spokesperson told TechCrunch.

SAN ANTONIO — Tesla started robotaxi rides in San Antonio at 5 a.m. on November 9, in a service area of about 274 square miles, its largest at launch. Local reports said the Model Ys carried no safety driver; Tesla's own post didn't say. San Antonio is Tesla's 5th robotaxi city in Texas, after Austin, Dallas, Houston and Fort Worth. Waymo already serves San Antonio too, and Alphabet says Waymo now runs in 15 major US cities.

The Carveyance take

Waymo sent its fix to its whole fleet in 12 days, by software, something no carmaker recalling steel parts could do. NHTSA is asking about the other half of that promise: whether a fix that's easy to send is also easy to prove. Waymo says the answer has been yes since March. Now it has to show the regulator the data.

What to watch: Waymo's formal answer to NHTSA, and how the agency's next monthly crash data treats Tesla's newest cities.

Enthusiasts · Rimac and Lotus

Rimac's numbers come from Mate Rimac's own video, reported November 11 · Horse revealed its V8 November 10 · the Lotus Type 135 is due in 2028, and its name isn't confirmed

Rimac Ends the Nevera at 71 Cars, and Lotus Shows the Hybrid V8 for Its Next Supercar

One of the most capable electric hypercars ever built ends at just over a third of the cars Rimac planned. Lotus's answer for the same buyers is a twin-turbo V8 with electric help.

ZAGREB, Croatia — Rimac will stop building the Nevera after 71 cars, 51 Neveras and 20 Nevera Rs, Mate Rimac said in a video on Instagram, widely reported on November 11, though a Dutch site, Autoblog.nl, had the 71-car figure in October. Rimac had planned 150 Neveras and 40 Nevera Rs, so it built about 37% of the 190 it intended. The last 10 Nevera Rs are being built now, with deliveries due by the end of the year. The Nevera cost €2 million at its launch in 2021, about $2.4 million at the time and about $3 million in today's money. It wasn't for lack of speed: in 2025 the Nevera R reached 268 mph (431.45 km/h) and ran from 0 to 400 km/h and back to a stop in 25.79 seconds, 2 of 24 records it set that year. "I think it is still a pretty good achievement. It's the most sold electric hypercar in the world," Rimac said. "And without that, there wouldn't be the Tourbillon today; there wouldn't be this factory." And: "So, it did its job." The Tourbillon is the 1,800 PS (1,775 hp) hybrid V16 Bugatti that Rimac's company now builds.

LONDON — The day before, Horse Powertrain, the Renault and Geely joint venture, revealed the W40, a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 that makes more than 500 kW (about 670 hp) and 800 Nm (590 lb-ft) and weighs 200 kg (441 lb). Its first home is the Lotus Type 135, a hybrid supercar due in 2028 with more than 1,000 hp combined, driven through a new 8-speed dual-clutch transmission. It will be the first Lotus with a V8 since the Esprit, which ended production in 2004 with a 3.5-liter twin-turbo V8. Lotus hasn't confirmed the new car's name. "They somehow just don't like the smoothness of EVs," Lotus chief executive Feng Qingfeng told Automotive News Europe in May, explaining why buyers at the top of the market want engines.

The Carveyance take

The Nevera did almost everything an engineer could ask of a car and too little of what a collector asks of one. At €2 million (about $2.4 million at launch), buyers wanted sound, a reason to keep it and a story to tell, and the quickest car on paper turned out to be easier to admire than to want. Lotus is betting its next buyer wants 1,000 hp and a V8 to hear while using it.

What to watch: what Lotus calls the Type 135, and what it charges for it.

Safety Notices

The week's 5 biggest recalls for drivers. Repairs are free, and you can check any car by its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, though the BMW recall won't show up there until December 25.

BMW: park outside until a new repair is ready
720,796 BMWs from the 2012–2018 model years, including the 2012–2016 3 Series sedan, the 2013–2017 X3 and the 2012–2016 5 Series, all covered by the 2024 water-pump recall. The pump's electrical connector can let in moisture and short circuit, which raises the risk of a fire even when the car is parked and off. Owners should park outside and away from buildings and other vehicles. The new repair is still being developed, and letters go out from December 25. NHTSA campaign 26V733, which replaces 24V608.
Honda Pilot, Acura MDX and TLX: power steering can cut out
635,808 vehicles: 383,110 Honda Pilots from the 2023–2025 model years, 177,100 Acura MDXs from 2022–2024 and 75,598 Acura TLXs from 2021–2025. The power-steering software can divide by 0 in a calculation for the driver-attention monitor, and it was set to cut the steering assist when that happens. The fault occurs while the car is driving straight. Honda has 146 warranty claims and 1 injury, and no crashes. Dealers will reprogram the steering control unit, and owner letters go out December 14. NHTSA campaign 26V721.
Ford Explorer Police Interceptor: map lights that won't turn off
33,578 Police Interceptors from the 2026–2027 model years. A false command in the overhead console can turn on the map lights and keep them from being switched off, which can distract the driver or cause glare. Dealers will replace the console on vehicles built before July 9, 2026, and inspect later ones. NHTSA campaign 26V726.
Harley-Davidson touring bikes: neutral shown while in gear
21,643 motorcycles from the 2026 model year, in the Street Glide and Road Glide families. The engine control module can report neutral when the bike is in gear, so it can move forward when the rider doesn't expect it. Dealers will replace the gear-position sensor, and owner letters go out November 16. NHTSA campaign 26V730.
Ford Maverick Hybrid: a loose battery cable
8,650 Maverick Hybrids from the 2022 model year. The terminal on the positive 12-volt battery cable can come loose or detach, which can cut drive power, power brake assist, power steering assist or the exterior lights. Dealers will replace the cable, and owner letters go out November 23. NHTSA campaign 26V724.

Also That Week

6 more stories worth knowing, in brief.

Road safety · NHTSA

Early estimate, released November 10 · final figures come later

US Road Deaths Fell 2.5% in the First Half of 2026

WASHINGTON — An estimated 16,750 people died in crashes on American roads from January to June, down from 17,175 a year earlier, NHTSA said on November 10, even though Americans drove 0.8% more miles. That puts the death rate at 1.02 per 100 million vehicle miles, down from 1.05, which NHTSA called a "near-record low." Deaths fell only 0.2% in the second quarter, and 35 states and Puerto Rico are projected to have had fewer. "Even with near-record low fatality rates, we will continue to work with a sense of urgency," said Jonathan Morrison, NHTSA's administrator.

Why it matters: the decline slowed in the spring, so the full-year number is still open.

Earnings · Nissan

Results November 11 · new business plan due in February 2027

Nissan Is Back to an Operating Profit, but Cuts Its Sales Outlook

YOKOHAMA, Japan — Nissan made an operating profit of ¥80.0 billion (about $506 million) from April to September, against a loss of ¥27.7 billion (about $175 million) a year earlier, on revenue of ¥6,072.0 billion (about $38.4 billion). It still lost ¥39.7 billion (about $251 million) overall, and nearly all of its operating profit came in the first quarter. It cut its full-year sales outlook from 3.15 million vehicles to between 2.97 million and 3 million, and sales in China fell 15%, Reuters reported. "China remains our most significant challenge, and we need to remain agile," said Ivan Espinosa, Nissan's chief executive.

Why it matters: Nissan's cost cuts are working, but it's selling fewer cars, and its new plan in February will have to show where growth comes from.

New factories · Scout Motors

Announced November 12 · series production in 2027 · first deliveries in 2028

Scout Starts Building Test Vehicles at Its South Carolina Plant

BLYTHEWOOD, S.C. — Scout Motors, Volkswagen's revived American brand, has started building validation vehicles of its Traveler SUV and Terra pickup at its new plant. They're for testing the tooling and the assembly process, not for sale. "What we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper," said Scott Keogh, Scout's chief executive. Series production follows in 2027, and the first customer deliveries are due in 2028. Scout says 87% of its 210,000 non-binding reservations are for the range-extended versions, which will come first.

Why it matters: it's the first sign the plant can build cars, and the reservations suggest buyers want the range extender more than the pure EV.

Factories · Stellantis

Agreement signed November 9 · expected to close by the end of 2026 · Unifor opposes the sale

Stellantis Agrees to Sell Its Brampton Plant to an Armored-Vehicle Maker

BRAMPTON, Ontario — Stellantis agreed on November 9 to sell its Brampton Assembly Plant, which built the Dodge Charger and Challenger and has been idle since 2023, to Roshel, a Canadian maker of armored vehicles, for an undisclosed amount. The deal still needs government and regulatory approvals. Roshel's founder said it plans a new center for advanced manufacturing there, without saying what it'll build. Unifor, which represents about 2,200 of the plant's workers, opposes the sale and says it breaks their contract. "Stellantis has betrayed our members with an underhanded deal to sell the plant," said Lana Payne, Unifor's president. Stellantis said it's "prepared to engage with Unifor to negotiate a settlement."

Why it matters: one of Canada's car plants is leaving the car business, in the middle of the country's tariff talks with Washington.

New markets · BYD

Launched November 13

BYD Brings Its Luxury Brand, Denza, to India

NEW DELHI — BYD launched Denza in India on November 13 with 2 imported EVs: the Z9 GT, a 3-motor shooting brake at Rs 1.57 crore (about $167,000) before registration and insurance, and the D9 minivan at Rs 90 lakh (about $96,000). Denza claims 1,156 hp for the Z9 GT, 0 to 100 km/h (62 mph) in 2.7 seconds and charging at up to 1,500 kW. It'll be sold in its own showrooms in 6 cities, separate from BYD's. "India is an important market in Denza's global journey," said Ketsu Zhang, BYD India's managing director.

Why it matters: China's carmakers are taking their premium brands into markets where Western luxury brands have had the top end mostly to themselves.

Robotaxis · Tesla

Reported by Electrek November 13 · deliveries estimated from December in Austin

Tesla Opens Cybercab Orders, With a Required $299 Monthly Subscription

AUSTIN, Texas — Tesla invited selected customers to order the Cybercab, its 2-seat car without a steering wheel or pedals, Electrek reported on November 13. The price is $29,990 plus a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and buyers must pay for a $299-a-month "Autonomy Subscription." It's offered only to people inside Tesla's robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, and Tesla estimates the first deliveries in Austin from December. The order page says: "Subscription and regular vehicle maintenance required to operate."

Why it matters: it's a car you can buy but use only inside the maker's service area, and only while you keep paying the subscription.

Since Last Week

Where last week's stories went next.

Follow-up · Tesla Cybertruck

In a post on X overnight into November 9, Musk said, as quoted by Electrek, that "the Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate" and that Tesla would "have to return deposits for a lot of people" before the Texas line comes out. On November 11 he changed the timing: "In order to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog, production will be extended through the end of summer 2027." Meanwhile, Tesla stopped taking orders for every version except the Cyberbeast and raised its price $7,500, to $109,990. Kelley Blue Book estimates Americans bought 20,237 Cybertrucks last year. Unplugged Performance, a California tuner, offered to take over building the truck; Tesla hasn't answered publicly. Read last week's story

Follow-up · Tesla Assisted Driving

Finland's transport agency, Traficom, recognized the provisional Dutch type approval of Tesla Assisted Driving, the renamed FSD, on November 10, making Finland the 11th EU country to allow it. It's a national decision that doesn't commit Finland's vote on approval for the whole EU, expected in December at the earliest. "The driver is still driving the car even if they are not physically touching its controls," said Jukka Juhola, a senior specialist at Traficom. Read last week's story

Follow-up · New-car prices

Last week's "what to watch" arrived on November 10: Americans paid a record $51,109 on average for a new vehicle in October, Kelley Blue Book said, up 1.3% from September and 2.1% from a year earlier. Incentives were 6.8% of the price, and the average EV sold for $56,220. "The average is telling us as much about product mix as it is about affordability," said Erin Keating, an executive analyst at Cox Automotive, noting that 3 of the 5 best-selling segments sold well below the average. Read last week's sales story

Follow-up · Fuel prices

The national average for regular fell below $4 a gallon on November 10 for the first time since July, and it was $3.81 on November 16, AAA said, down from $4.01 a week earlier and $4.33 a month ago, though still 74 cents more than a year ago. Lower demand after the summer and the end of daylight saving time helped push it down.

Follow-up · The Canada tariff

There was no change this week to the 50% tariff on Canadian-built cars set for January 1. On November 15, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada could turn to Chinese carmakers to build cars there if the talks with Washington don't protect its auto industry: "Canada is going to move forward either way." APEC's leaders meet in Shenzhen, China, on November 18 and 19, though no Trump–Carney meeting has been formally announced. Read last week's Brief

Worth Watching

Not big stories yet, but they could be.

GM moves to Nasdaq, November 17
GM's shares move from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq on Tuesday, under the same GM ticker. GM says the move makes it eligible for the Nasdaq-100 index.
The LA Auto Show, November 20 to 29
The industry and media day is November 19, and the show opens to the public November 20 at the Los Angeles Convention Center. It's the last big American show of the year for new models.
Volkswagen's talks, November 24
VW and IG Metall open new in-house wage talks on November 24. Staff who want the extra €55,000 (about $62,000) on top of a buyout have to register interest by December 4, according to Manager Magazin.
Britain's 2030 EV target
Last week we said a decision on cutting the share of new cars that must be zero-emission in 2030 could come soon. As of November 15, the government hadn't published one. The current rule is 80%.
Europe's vote on Tesla Assisted Driving
The vote on approving the renamed FSD for the whole EU is expected in December at the earliest, and it needs a qualified majority of member states. Finland became the 11th country to allow it on its own this week.

News Versus Noise

How solid is each story? Our ledger for the week.

Confirmed
Toyota's Scion announcement and the KEI-01's equipment and Indiana plans. Honda's new plant, its results and the hybrid-only CR-V. Mercedes' investment freeze, from its own interview with employees. The BMW recall and NHTSA's warning, and the 4 other recalls. Benchmark's and CAAM's October figures. NHTSA's inquiry into Waymo's recall. Tesla's San Antonio service area. Horse's V8. Nissan's results, NHTSA's half-year estimate, Scout's test builds, Denza's Indian launch and the Brampton agreement. Ford's Mach-E battery figures, as Ford's own data, which no one outside Ford has audited.
Reported, not confirmed
Rimac's 71 Neveras, from Mate Rimac's video as reported by others; a Dutch site counted 1 fewer standard Nevera. VW's new buyout offer, from Manager Magazin. The plants where BMW canceled shifts, from unnamed company sources. Tesla's Cybercab orders, from Electrek. Outlets' identification of the KEI-01 as a Toyota Pixis Truck, or Daihatsu Hijet. That Tesla's San Antonio rides have no safety driver, which local outlets reported but Tesla's post didn't say. A Global News report that 700 to 1,000 Brampton workers could return under Roshel.
Plans without dates
The KEI-01's price and any retail sales. The models Honda's new Ohio plant will build. BMW's new repair. Whether Mercedes closes a German plant, and which one. Which car Roshel will build in Brampton, if any.
Not final yet
Mercedes' talks with IG Metall. The Brampton sale, which needs approvals and is opposed by Unifor. EU-wide approval of Tesla Assisted Driving. NHTSA's review of Waymo's fix. And the half-year road-death figures, which are an early estimate.
Noise
"Lotus's first V8": the Esprit V8 was in production until 2004. "BMW recalls cars after 10 fires": NHTSA and BMW count about 10 incidents that "relate, or may relate," and neither calls them fires. "Scout has started production": these are validation vehicles, not cars for sale. Rimac's 71-car figure as news broken this week: a Dutch site reported it in October. And the €2.5 million (about $2.8 million) price some outlets gave the Nevera R: Rimac says €2.3 million (about $2.6 million).
